<style id="fareharbor-marketing-block-generateblocks-pro-classic-menu-inline-css">
/*
 * Per-block stylesheet for `generateblocks-pro/classic-menu` (scoped to `.legal-menu`).
 *
 * Enqueued by `Theme::register_block_descendant_styles()` via
 * `wp_enqueue_block_style()`, which lazy-loads this file only when a
 * `generateblocks-pro/classic-menu` block renders on the page (and into
 * the block editor iframe when the block is inserted).
 *
 * Why this lives here instead of in the GenerateBlocks Global Class
 * registry: GB Pro's classic-menu block renders its `<ul>/<li>/<a>`
 * through `wp_nav_menu()`, so the migration cannot apply a Global Class
 * to each inner element. The list-item and link rules below are
 * therefore expressed as descendant selectors scoped to the registered
 * `.legal-menu` wrapper class (the `<ul>`), which DOES have its own
 * entry in `GenerateBlocksGlobalClassRegistry.php`.
 *
 * Ported from the legacy `.sidebar-nav .button` rules in
 * `old-site/theme/scss/layout/_sidebar.scss`.
 */

.legal-menu li:not(:last-child) {
	margin-bottom: var(--space-xxs);
}

.legal-menu a {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	width: 100%;
	min-height: 2.5rem;
	padding: var(--space-s) var(--space-horz-m);
	font-size: var(--font-size-m);
	font-weight: var(--font-weight-medium);
	color: var(--color-text-weak);
	text-decoration: none;
	border-radius: var(--border-radius-s);
	transition: var(--transition-slowly);
}

.legal-menu a:hover,
.legal-menu a:focus-visible {
	color: var(--color-text);
}

.legal-menu a[aria-current="page"] {
	color: var(--color-text);
	background-color: var(--color-border);
}

/*# sourceURL=https://marketing.fareharbor.com/wp-content/themes/fareharbor-marketing/styles/blocks/legal-menu.css */
</style>

<style id="fareharbor-marketing-block-generateblocks-text-inline-css">
/*
 * Per-block stylesheet for `generateblocks/text` (scoped to `.customer-story-body`).
 *
 * Enqueued by `Theme::register_block_descendant_styles()` via
 * `wp_enqueue_block_style()`, which lazy-loads this file only when a
 * `generateblocks/text` block renders on the page (and into the block
 * editor iframe when the block is inserted).
 *
 * Customer-story body copy is parsed into `generateblocks/text` blocks
 * (not `core/heading` / `core/paragraph`). Heading size overrides for
 * long-form story copy belong here — not in a file named after the
 * inner block type.
 *
 * Scope: every selector below MUST begin with `.customer-story-body`.
 */

.customer-story-body h2 {
	font-size: 1.75rem;
}

@media (min-width: 768px) {
	.customer-story-body h2 {
		font-size: 2rem;
	}
}

.customer-story-body h3 {
	font-size: 1.5rem;
}

/*# sourceURL=https://marketing.fareharbor.com/wp-content/themes/fareharbor-marketing/styles/blocks/customer-story-body.css */
</style>

</style>
<style id="fareharbor-marketing-card-grid-inline-css">
/*
 * Shared card descendant styles for `.card-title`, `.card-image`, and
 * `.card-badges` wrappers.
 *
 * Registered on `core/post-title`, `core/post-featured-image`, and
 * `core/post-terms` via `Theme::register_block_descendant_styles()` so
 * `wp_enqueue_block_style()` lazy-loads whenever any card inner block
 * renders — whether inside a migrated GB query looper
 * (`GridHelpers::card_template()`), a PHP-rendered customer-story card
 * (`Theme::render_customer_story_card()`), or a blog-post slider slide.
 *
 * Wrapper layout (`.card`, `.card-content`, `.card-badges` flex rhythm,
 * etc.) lives in GenerateBlocks Pro Global Classes. This file owns only
 * the descendant rules core blocks render but cannot class.
 */

.card-title a {
	color: var(--link-color);
	text-decoration: none;
	transition: color var(--transition-slowly);
}

.card-title a:hover,
.card-title a:focus-visible {
	color: var(--link-color-hover);
}

.card-image img {
	display: block;
	width: 100%;
	height: auto;
	aspect-ratio: var(--img-aspect-ratio);
	object-fit: cover;
	border-radius: var(--border-radius-picture);
}

.card-badges a {
	display: inline-block;
	padding: var(--badge-padding-block) var(--badge-padding-inline);
	border-radius: var(--border-radius-pill);
	background-color: var(--wp--preset--color--surface-green);
	color: var(--wp--preset--color--secondary);
	font-size: var(--badge-font-size);
	font-weight: var(--font-weight-bold);
	text-transform: uppercase;
	text-decoration: none;
}

/*
 * Cards emit `core/post-terms` with an empty separator, so the separator
 * span carries no text; hide it outright so it never adds stray flex
 * spacing between the stacked pills.
 */
.card-badges .wp-block-post-terms__separator {
	display: none;
}

/*# sourceURL=https://marketing.fareharbor.com/wp-content/themes/fareharbor-marketing/styles/blocks/card-grid.css */
</style>

<style id="fareharbor-marketing-block-fareharbor-testimonials-row-inline-css">
/*
 * Per-block stylesheet for `fareharbor/testimonials-row`.
 *
 * Enqueued by `Theme::register_block_descendant_styles()` via
 * `wp_enqueue_block_style()`, which lazy-loads this file only when a
 * `fareharbor/testimonials-row` block renders on the page (and into the
 * block editor iframe when the block is inserted).
 *
 * Why this lives here instead of in the GenerateBlocks Global Class registry
 * (`client-mu-plugins/fareharbor-gb-abilities/includes/`
 * `GenerateBlocksGlobalClassRegistry.php`): the card markup (linked logo,
 * quote, headshot, attribution) is emitted by this block's `render.php`
 * as raw HTML with BEM-style classes. Those classes are not separate GB
 * blocks an author can chip onto, so the styling travels with the block.
 *
 * Legacy sources:
 *   - `old-site/theme/scss/rows/_testimonials.scss` — logo + headshot rules
 *   - `old-site/theme/templates/blocks/testimonials-row.twig` — markup shape
 *   - `old-site/theme/scss/base/_util.scss` — `.stack-l` / `.stack-2xs`
 *     vertical rhythm (now GB Global Classes on the emitted markup)
 *
 * Vertical spacing between logo / quote / attribution is owned by the
 * `.stack-l` Global Class on `.testimonial-card`. This file resets the
 * browser-default margins on `figure`, `blockquote`, and `p` that would
 * otherwise stack on top of that gap.
 */

.testimonial-card {
	margin: 0;
}

.testimonials-row-logo {
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	height: 4rem;
}

.testimonials-logo-image {
	max-width: 144px;
	max-height: 100%;
}

.testimonial-quote {
	margin: 0;
	padding: 0;
	border: 0;
}

.testimonial-quote > p {
	margin: 0;
}

.testimonial-quote > p::before {
	content: open-quote;
}

.testimonial-quote > p::after {
	content: close-quote;
}

.testimonial-headshot {
	margin: 0;
}

.testimonial-headshot img {
	width: 4rem;
	height: 4rem;
	object-fit: cover;
	border-radius: var(--border-radius-circle);
}

.testimonial-attribution > p {
	margin: 0;
}

.attribution-name {
	font-weight: var(--font-weight-bold);
}

/*# sourceURL=https://marketing.fareharbor.com/wp-content/themes/fareharbor-marketing/styles/blocks/fareharbor-testimonials-row.css */
</style>
